main_body: Two-storey half-timbered tavern: a large tiled hip roof over a plaster and timber front wall with shuttered windows, a plank door and a hanging beer sign
top_band: Orange terracotta tile roof slope, rows 0-43 (light orange tiles with darker rows), ending in a dark brown eave line at rows 42-44
evidence: Down a middle column the roof slope (tiles, rows 0-43) is a large visible top surface. It ends in a dark brown eave edge at rows 42-44, which casts a shadow onto the plaster wall (rows 44-95). The wall has timber framing, a door with an inset frame and lintel, and shuttered windows with sills. This matches the Beodeul house references, where a tiled roof sits above a front wall. No isometric side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 tile tones, with per-tile highlights and dark seams between the rows. The plaster wall is speckled in 3-4 tones. The timber is dark brown, and the shutters, glowing windows, door planks, iron straps, sign and stone base all carry several tones. Outlines are tinted dark brown or material-toned rather than black. Tile density matches or exceeds the references, so it holds up beside them.
